measurement: scripts/check-kiwi-inventory-ratchet.py imports infra/kiwi/sync.py by path (the same module scripts/tests/test_kiwi_sync.py loads) and calls scan_repository(), so the number the gate reads is the number the test suite counts — two readers of one scanner, not two scanners

floors.label: *Test.kt files the scanner classifies as runnable
floors.note:
This is the only metric in the repository that was still a literal inside a test assertion, and it cost two merge conflicts in one day: abf88fc2 and 4733aec4 each added a test class and each raised the number by hand, independently, to the same value. The cost is the point. A number edited in a test file is a number two branches edit, and the merge that reconciles them resolves a number rather than a decision.

What the bound is for, precisely, because it is easy to read as more than it is. The skip list is now derived — `unjustified_skips` re-derives each entry from the file that earns it — and there is an exhaustiveness check that every `*Test.kt` is either in the inventory or justified-skip. Neither of those can catch a regression in the *predicate*, because both ask it the same question. The predicate's own controls are synthetic (`test_parameterized_test_counts_as_a_test` and friends), so they do not need this either.

What is left is narrow and worth keeping: this fires when the inventory moves in a way no synthetic control anticipated. It caught the two merges above, which is the whole argument for it. It is NOT a coverage claim, and a run where it fires is not evidence that anything regressed — it is a prompt to look.

Raising `max` costs one line in this file, where the reason travels with the measurement. That is the entire difference from the assertion it replaces.

Raised 370 -> 380 with the measurement, on a merge that added eight test classes at once (reminders, proposals, profile, notes). Worth recording that the gate caught this without anyone reading the diff: `measured` was still 360, and the drift check reported a floor file describing a different commit. That is the case the number-in-a-test could not produce at all. Measured 375 -> 381 on 2026-10-07, entirely from the six calendar-sync scenario carriers (one scenario per file — `link_index` rejects two in one) plus their helpers, none of which is a Kiwi TCMS case and none of which the scanner skips. The ceiling is 380 and the inventory is now 381, so the scanner is *above* its own ceiling: that is the direction the ratchet exists to stop, and the honest response is to raise the ceiling with the attribution recorded here rather than to delete tests to fit it.

Raised 385 -> 400 with the measurement. The attachment branch adds ten test classes (viewer routing, MIME classification, FileOpener outcome, zoom, three spotlight geometry/state-machine classes, the v40->v41 migration, the backup annotation round-trip, and annotation anchor resolution) taking the counter 382 -> 394. Six slots of headroom, less than the growth it absorbs, so the bound still asks the question rather than becoming a formality. The attribution is here, next to the number, which is the entire reason this file exists — a number edited inside a test assertion was a number two branches edited independently, and the merge between them resolved a number rather than a decision.

+2 on 2026-10-08 for `CapabilityFlagTest` and `AndroidNotifierTest`, re-measured after merging 26316f2b (attachments). Both are gates that can fail; nothing was skipped to reach this number.

floors.label: *Test.kt files the scanner classifies as non-runnable (abstract bases and helpers)
floors.note:
Moved here from `ScanRepositoryTest` so both inventory numbers live in one place.

The ceiling is a backstop, not the primary check. `unjustified_skips` asks whether each entry is still justified by its file, which is the question that matters; a large skip list with every entry justified means the predicate began rejecting real tests, and the per-entry check cannot see that on its own because it would be asking the broken predicate for confirmation.

known_gaps: Both numbers move whenever a test class is added, which is the intended direction: this ratchet caps the inventory from above so a filter regression that *inflates* it is caught, and the growth in the normal direction is a one-line edit here rather than a merge conflict in a test.
